messages:
ana: Deploybot flagged our canary for v3.2.1, auto-promotion blocked. Notifying release owners.

deploybot: [ALERT] Publication quarantine: repository=infra/web:tag=v3.2.1
Reason: tag collision detected (multiple digests for same tag within 2m). Provenance attestation present for one digest only.
Action: manual digest pin OR republish with unique tag.

kevin: That was my local test accidentally pushing the same tag after CI. Sorry team.

ryan: No worries. We need to decide: pin canary to the verified digest or force a republish with a new tag?

tanya: Prefer pinning if cosign verifies the CI image. Republish will delay stable rollout and needs another canary window.

ana: Can you fetch both digests and confirm which one is signed?

kevin: Ran `aws ecr describe-images --repository-name infra/web --image-ids imageTag=v3.2.1` -> digests: sha256:1111aaaa... and sha256:2222bbbb...

ryan: I verified: `cosign verify --key ksm://proj/... sha256:1111aaaa...` -> OK (CI key). `cosign verify sha256:2222bbbb...` -> verification FAILED.

deploybot: [INFO] Suggestion: pin route=canary to digest=sha256:1111aaaa... ; annotate release notes with quarantine reason.

ana: If we pin, we should also add a release note entry: "Canary pinned to digest sha256:1111aaaa due to duplicated tag; second digest lacked provenance."

kevin: I'm happy to republish a test image with `:v3.2.1-dev-kevin` if you prefer to avoid pinning, but that will require a fresh cosign step.

ryan: For speed let's pin the canary now, roll traffic for 20m, then decide. If anything odd, rollback plan is immediate unpin and revert route to previous stable digest.

ana: I'll approve the pin. Kevin, please follow up with a PR to CI to fail on duplicate-tag detection. Add a check that `describe-images` returns <=1 digest for a given tag during push.

kevin: Will do. Also I'll clean up my accidental push (delete the unverified digest) after we've confirmed stability to avoid confusing mirrors.

ryan: How do we perform the pin via the release API?

ana: Use: `POST /api/releases/789/actions` body `{ "action": "pin_digest", "digest": "sha256:1111aaaa...", "route": "canary" }` (needs release-owner approval).

kevin: I just submitted the request and tagged @ana for approval.

deploybot: [INFO] Action submitted: pin_digest by kevin for release=789. Awaiting approval.

ana: Approved. Proceed.

deploybot: [INFO] Canary route pinned to sha256:1111aaaa... Traffic shift scheduled: +10% every 5m up to 50%. Change window: 45m.

ryan: I'll monitor errors and latency for the next two traffic increments. If error-rate > 2% or p50 latency regresses > 200ms, we will revert.

kevin: After canary stable, I'll republish a corrected artifact for stable if needed and update the release notes with new stable tag and reason.

ana: I've added release note bullet: "Hold during automated check for duplicate tag; canary pinned to digest sha256:1111aaaa (CI-signed). Follow-up: CI to enforce unique tag policy; dev pushes to use ephemeral tags."

tanya: Also scheduling a 1hr change window at 21:00 UTC in case we need to republish and re-run canary.

ryan: Thanks. If canary passes the 30m observation, we'll promote and close.

deploybot: [REMINDER] Please do not delete images until after release closure to preserve audit trail.

kevin: Understood. I'll avoid deletion until we confirm. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

tanya: I'll post final status when the canary completes. :white_check_mark:
